Can the pin even express the tail? Phase-binned basis capture

Fraction of demo-chunk variance inside span(U) (normalized zero-padded H=50 chunks, the flow's training target), by chunk-start phase and per task. Pooled capture looks healthy because between-task variance is easy; the within-task numbers are what steering precision uses.

The two failing settles live exactly in the weak cells: right mid-flight and stop capture 0.43, left 0.51–0.57. Roughly half the tail movement is invisible to the command channel on the flat basis — the box measured the same structure (flat 0.34 vs mh16 0.81 on its stop-segment definition).

Is the failing tail command-content or expressiveness? Both — split by arm

Served command vs the nearest demo state's own command (clog_analysis, chunk-displacement metres), per arm and side:

gmm / right10/10 strict59%0.210.28 on-manifold

  • Each twin is command-accurate exactly on the side it wins (0.21–0.44 m mean error on wins vs 0.50–0.57 m on losses).
  • gmm-left is wrong ON the demo manifold (0.72 m error at <0.15 m from demo states): command content, not covariate shift.
  • ctl-right drifts off-manifold then commands worsen (69% of replans >0.3 m off, error 0.59 m out there): accumulated mid-flight imprecision, the known restoring-field gap.

Reading

  • The settle failure is over-determined: the flat K=5 basis can only express ~43–57% of the within-task tail movement (table above), and the head's tail commands are also wrong in-span. Fixing either alone is unlikely to close a 0/10.
  • The measured, already-validated lever for expressiveness is the multi-horizon basis (mh16): box finding, stop-segment capture 0.34 → 0.81. Its rebuild recipe exists (mh_basis_audit.py / RESEARCH_LOG 2026-08-13); tail-weighting and per-band soft pins stay rejected as regime patches.
  • π(o) came back degenerate (one component, 0.74–1.0 everywhere): the MDN behaves as heteroscedastic regression. Whatever helps its right-settle is not mixture routing — worth the σ-by-phase probe before crediting a mechanism.
  • Seed replication for both twins is still required before "endgame ownership flipped on the head axis" becomes a claim (gen16 precedent: ownership flipped on seed alone).
